requirement: The bundled skills MUST direct agents to make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each of many sites, such as a convention every validation function follows; to use `{impl}` instead when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole; and to mark with `{impl}` the code that carries out any obligation of a distributed requirement that its sites do not uphold.
rationale:
The requirement has three directive clauses for the bundled skills. Skills are text assets, so a test adequately checks them by asserting that the guidance is present in the right place. The single test `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_make_a_requirement_distributed_only_for_per_site_obligations]` does that.

It takes the `## Do` section of the habeas skill's distributed-requirements reference. It gets that through `distributed_reference()` and `section(...)`, which cuts the section out and collapses its whitespace. It then uses `assert_text`, which panics if a phrase is missing. It asserts two sentences:

1. "Make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each site; when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole, use `{impl}` there." This covers clause 1 (distribute only for per-site obligations) and clause 2 (use `{impl}` instead when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole).
2. "Separate obligations each site upholds from obligations particular code carries out, and mark that code `{impl}`." This covers clause 3 (mark with `{impl}` the code that carries out obligations the sites do not uphold).

I read `assets/skills/habeas/references/distributed-requirements.md`. Both bullets are in its `Do` section, and the intro there gives the "many sites, such as a convention every validation function follows" framing. That is the implementation named by the `:impl:` anchor in `md/requirements/cli.md`. The test fails if either directive is removed or weakened, because every phrase must be present in that section.

Two minor points do not amount to gaps:
- The "many sites" and "convention every validation function follows" wording sits in the intro, which this test does not assert. Both are illustrative ("such as") context, and the operative directive is the `Do` bullet that the test does check.
- The test covers only the habeas skill's reference. The implementation anchor and my search found the guidance only in that reference, so no other skill carries these directives.

No fixme acknowledgments apply, and none are needed.
